newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast police arrest mutineers on German ship.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast police arrest mutineers on German ship.

text.p: A mutiny on a German-owned ship ended on Friday when police in Ivory Coast boarded the vessel and arrested crew members suspected of killing two ship officers, Abidjan port officials said.
A port duty officer told Reuters the 4,455-ton MV Janna, registered in Antigua and Barbuda, docked on Friday and was quickly boarded by police.
"Even the security minister was here. The people killed had been thrown overboard. Police arrested those suspected of doing it and took them to the port police station," he said.
He did not know the number of people arrested.
The cisrcumstances of the ship's arrival in Abidjan after travelling from Port Harcourt, Nigeria, were not clear and there was no immediate police comment.
Lloyds shipping service said in London on Wednesday that two people were missing and feared dead after a mutiny by two crew members on the ship in the Gulf of Guinea off the West African coast.
Lloyd's, quoting coastguard personnel, said the mutineers had eventually been overpowered and locked up.
The ship, which was thought to have a crew of nine, was travelling from Nigeria to Takoradi in Ghana when it issued a distress signal late on Tuesday.
Lloyd's said the ship's master and chief engineer were missing and believed dead. The remainder of the crew locked themselves in the wheelhouse and bridge for safety.
The ship is owned by a German company.
